subject: KV cache fragmentation escalation — customer latency event (SUP-4391 / PM-2025-02-11)
related_account: Dedicated customer (name redacted in internal thread)
body:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 8:17 AM PST
Subject: KV cache fragmentation escalation — customer latency event (SUP-4391 / PM-2025-02-11)

Team — escalating after yesterday’s customer-facing latency event. This isn’t a one-off; fragmentation + allocator churn is showing up in multiple pools under burst/mixed-length traffic.

Links:
- SUP-4391 (Dedicated customer p99 spikes): SUP-4391
- Postmortem draft: PM-2025-02-11 “burst tail latency + KV fragmentation”

I need alignment today on:
1) Priority: this should be P0 for Runtime + SRE until we have a credible mitigation/rollout plan.
2) Staffing: Omar/Noah — who is on point for allocator/compaction work vs. eviction policy vs. scheduler hooks? Sean/Rafael — who owns canary + SLO/alerts?
3) Timeline: proposal for an instrumentation-first sprint + a flag-guarded remediation path. I’m expecting an end-of-week plan w/ milestones and explicit rollback levers.

Immediate ask: please reply with (a) current risk assessment for the next 72h and (b) what we can safely do now (routing, admission control, cache limits) without causing collateral damage.

Mateo
VP Engineering, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 9:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: KV cache fragmentation escalation — customer latency event (SUP-4391 / PM-2025-02-11)

Risk next 72h:
- Elevated. The same pattern is present in us-west hosted + the affected Dedicated pool (bursty arrivals + long-context mix). If we get another burst during peak we’ll see p99 timeouts again.

Safe mitigations (now):
- Keep the temporary admission control tightening in the dedicated pool (we already adjusted last night). This reduces incidence but impacts throughput.
- Route long-context traffic away from the “hot” pool when possible (we can do this for hosted; dedicated is more limited).
- Set a short-term cap on max concurrent sequences per GPU in that pool (trade-off: throughput).

What we need from Runtime:
- Instrumentation we can alert on. Right now we infer fragmentation indirectly; we need explicit allocator failure counters and a fragmentation ratio/holes measure, broken down by pool.
- A plan for compaction/eviction behind a flag + a canary target.

Rafael and I can own the canary process and oncall readiness once we have metric names/threshold candidates.

Sean
SRE Lead


From: Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 10:11 AM PST
Subject: Re: KV cache fragmentation escalation — customer latency event (SUP-4391 / PM-2025-02-11)

Agree this is P0.

Proposed ownership (Runtime):
- Omar: allocator refactor + compaction engine path (block map + move semantics) + feature-flag plumbing.
- Noah: architecture/contract review (scheduler <-> cache), concurrency/safety model, and design doc/ADR shepherding.

Dependencies / additional owners needed:
- Scheduler integration: we need Sofia (or Julian) to wire cache-pressure signals + backpressure hooks. I can’t do that safely without scheduler ownership.
- Kernel safety: I want Grace/Yuki to sanity check stream sync requirements for any “move” operations.

Timeline proposal (aggressive but realistic):
- Week 1: instrumentation + baseline (fragmentation ratio + allocator failures + per-request attribution) + perf reproduction scenario in lab.
- Week 2-3: allocator block map abstraction (no behavior change) + initial eviction policy v1.
- Week 4: compaction engine behind runtime flag, with budget enforcement (cap worst-case overhead).
- Week 5: canary in one region + one dedicated pool.

Immediate: I can start with metrics/structured logging and land a PR quickly. That unblocks SRE alerting even before compaction exists.

Omar
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime


From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 11:26 AM PST
Subject: Re: KV cache fragmentation escalation — customer latency event (SUP-4391 / PM-2025-02-11)

+1 on instrumentation first.

To make the canary safe we need (minimum):
- A rollback trigger list we all agree on (p99 regression threshold, allocator failures > X/min, OOMs, compaction time > budget).
- “Compaction events” in logs (with pool/model tags) so oncall can correlate p99 spikes.
- A dashboard slice by pool/region, because the bad behavior is not uniform.

Allison — can you help define the SLO-facing metrics/alert thresholds? We can mirror the tail-latency SLO but include fragmentation signals.

Also: please be explicit about what knobs are safe to change at runtime (cache size, admission control, eviction mode, compaction budget). We’ll bake those into the runbook.

Rafael Mendes
SRE (Runtime)


From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 1:03 PM PST
Subject: Re: KV cache fragmentation escalation — customer latency event (SUP-4391 / PM-2025-02-11)

From release side: if we’re going to iterate quickly + safely, we should plan for:
- Feature flag default OFF (per pool) with config gating (so we can canary by region/pool without a new build).
- A “kill switch” that hard-disables compaction if it misbehaves (one knob, not multiple).
- Backport strategy: if we land instrumentation and allocator refactor independently, we can ship those on the next stable train even if compaction slips.

If Runtime can commit to a PR sequence (metrics -> allocator refactor -> eviction -> compaction -> scheduler integration), we can line up the trains.

Connor
Release Engineering


From: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: KV cache fragmentation escalation — customer latency event (SUP-4391 / PM-2025-02-11)

I can help with the observability spec + thresholds, but I need Runtime to define:
- exact metric names + units (gauge vs counter) for fragmentation ratio, allocation failure, eviction rate, compaction bytes moved/time
- tag cardinality constraints (pool/region/model family ok; request_id not ok for metrics, but fine for logs/traces)

Initial threshold suggestion for canary (to refine after we have baselines):
- allocator failures: any sustained non-zero rate is paging (since it’s tightly coupled to tail latency + OOM)
- compaction overhead: budget must be enforced; alert if compaction time exceeds budget in consecutive intervals
- tail latency: p99 degradation > 10% for > 15 min = rollback candidate (unless explained by traffic shift)

Once we have baseline graphs, I’ll propose alert rules and help Rafael draft the runbook section.

Allison Grant
Observability Standards & Alerting


From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 6:06 PM PST
Subject: Re: KV cache fragmentation escalation — customer latency event (SUP-4391 / PM-2025-02-11)

Thanks all. Decisions + next steps:

Priority / program:
- This is P0 until we have (1) instrumentation + dashboards + runbook and (2) a flag-guarded remediation path to reduce fragmentation-driven tails.
- Track work under Linear ENG-2841.

Owners:
- Runtime implementation: Omar (allocator/compaction) + Noah (architecture + contract + review).
- SRE rollout + canary: Sean + Rafael.
- Observability spec/alerts: Allison (partnering w/ Logan’s team as needed).
- Release train/flag wiring: Connor.

Immediate (by EOD Tue):
- Omar/Noah: instrumentation PR plan (metric names, tags, logging) + an initial design outline covering move semantics + safety constraints.
- Sean/Rafael: proposed canary targets (one hosted region + one dedicated pool) and a short list of rollback triggers.

Timeline:
- Week 1 deliverable is metrics + baseline. We cannot keep guessing.
- After that: staged PRs as Connor outlined; everything behind a single kill-switch flag, default OFF.

Product/customer comms:
- Nikhil/Lauren: please treat this as “stability fix, no API behavior change.” We’ll update SUP-4391 with the timeline once we have the week-1 baseline and canary window.

Let’s do a 30 min check-in Monday 10:30a to confirm Week 1 scope and unblock dependencies.

Mateo
VP Engineering, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
